title: Zero locus of a section over a valuation base is relative Cartier
statement: Let A be a valuation ring, let f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) be proper, flat, and of finite presentation [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let X_0 be the integral closed fibre [def-pc-integral-scheme], let L be an invertible module on X [def-sc-invertible-module], and let s be a global section of L whose restriction to X_0 is nonzero. Then the zero scheme Z(s) [def-pc-zero-scheme] is a relative effective Cartier divisor on X over \operatorname{Spec}(A) [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], hence Z(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) is flat.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, Tag 0EX8, proof paragraph invoking Divisors Lemma fibre-Cartier

proof.text: The zero scheme Z(s) is locally principal by [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties](1): on an affine open U=Spec(B) of X where L is free on e and s|_U=a e, Z(s)\cap U=Spec(B/(a)). Its closed fibre is therefore affine-locally Spec(B_0/(\bar a)) with B_0=B\otimes_A\kappa and \bar a the image of a, i.e. Z(s)_0=Z(s|_{X_0}) as closed subschemes of X_0. Since s|_{X_0} is a nonzero section of the invertible module L|_{X_0} on the integral scheme X_0, [lem-pc-nonzero-section-integral-cartier] says that Z(s)_0=Z(s|_{X_0}) is an effective Cartier divisor on X_0. Let x be a point of Z(s), and let C be the closure of x in X; C\subseteq Z(s) since Z(s) is closed. The image f(C) is closed in Spec(A) by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] and nonempty (it contains f(x)); every nonempty closed subset of the local scheme Spec(A) contains the closed point, so some y\in C lies over the closed point. Thus y\in Z(s), y lies in the closed fibre, and x specializes to y. By the preceding paragraph Z(s)_0\subseteq X_0 is an effective Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of y, and f is flat and locally of finite presentation, so the local fibre-Cartier criterion [lem-pc-recd-fibre-cartier-local] gives an open neighbourhood U_y of y with Z(s)\cap U_y a relative effective Cartier divisor on U_y over Spec(A). Since x specializes to y, every open containing y contains x, so x\in U_y. Hence the opens U_y cover Z(s); together with the open X\setminus Z(s), on which the ideal of Z(s) is the unit ideal, they cover X, and being a relative effective Cartier divisor is local on X (effective Cartier is local, and flatness of Z(s)\to Spec(A) is local on Z(s)). So Z(s) is a relative effective Cartier divisor on X over Spec(A).

proof.text: By the definition [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], a relative effective Cartier divisor has flat structure morphism to Spec(A). Thus Z(s) → Spec(A) is flat.
